note.headline: 동아프리카 표준 36건이 한꺼번에 확정된 9월
note.subtitle: 2026년 9월 배포분 · 식품 관련 통보 182건
note.lead: 9월 식품 관련 통보 182건에서 눈여겨볼 흐름은 다섯 가지입니다.

themes.title: 동아프리카 5개국이 표준 36건을 한꺼번에 확정했습니다
themes.text: 부룬디·케냐·르완다·탄자니아·우간다가 공동으로 낸 통보가 36건으로 9월 전체의 5분의 1을 차지했습니다. 36건 모두 이전에 통보한 표준안이 확정됐다는 추가통보입니다. 어육 소시지·어류 통조림·냉동 랍스터 꼬리 등 수산물 규격 8건, 홍차·녹차·인스턴트 차 규격, 물엿·경질 사탕 등 당류 규격, 영양강화 백미·철분강화 콩 규격이 포함됐습니다.

themes.title: 농약·동물용의약품 잔류기준 통보가 이어졌습니다
themes.text: 중국이 식품 중 동물용의약품 142종의 잔류허용기준을 담은 국가표준안을 통보했습니다. 캐나다는 사이프로디닐·플루디옥소닐 잔류허용기준안을 내고 클로란트라닐리프롤 기준을 확정했습니다. 브라질은 농약 유효성분 모노그래프 25종을 한꺼번에 개정하는 결의안을 냈고, 우크라이나는 동물용의약품 잔류허용기준 설정 절차를 확정했습니다.

themes.title: 감미료·첨가물 기준과 영유아식 기준이 바뀌었습니다
themes.text: 홍콩은 식품 감미료 규정을 국제기준에 맞춰 개정하는 의견수렴을, 말레이시아는 감미료를 식품첨가물 정의에 넣는 개정안을 통보했습니다. 브라질은 식품첨가물·가공보조제 사용기준 개정안을 냈습니다. 유럽연합은 영유아용 곡류가공식품·이유식 중 푸란류 최대기준을 확정했습니다.

themes.title: 우크라이나가 EU 기준에 맞춘 식품 규정을 잇달아 냈습니다
themes.text: 우크라이나는 특수의료용도식품 조성요건, 체중조절용 식사대용식품, 천연광천수·샘물, 우유·유제품 요건 등 13건을 통보했습니다. 같은 내용 상당수를 SPS와 TBT로 함께 냈기 때문에 이번 호에서는 SPS 쪽만 싣고 비고에 표시했습니다.

themes.title: 가금·돼지 수입제한은 해제와 신규가 엇갈렸습니다
themes.text: 사우디아라비아는 폴란드 5개 주산 가금육·계란 수입 금지를 해제하고 영국산 금지도 풀었습니다. 반면 프랑스 멘에루아르주산은 새로 금지했습니다. 태국은 아프리카돼지열병을 이유로 핀란드산 돼지 수입·경유를 일시 중단했습니다.

items.ko: 특수의료용도식품 조성요건 명령안 개정
items.orig: The draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of the Requirements for the Composition of Food for Special Medical Purposes”
items.products: Food for special medical purposes
items.note: 같은 명령안을 TBT로도 통보(G/TBT/N/UKR/401)
items.desc: The draft Order provides for the approval of mandatory requirements for the composition of food for special medical purposes.The draft Requirements classify food for special medical purposes into three categories: nutritionally complete food with a standard nutrient formulation; nutritionally complete food with a nutrient-adapted formulation specific for a disease, disorder or medical condition; and nutritionally incomplete food with a standard or nutrient-adapted formulation, which is not suitable to be used as the sole source of nourishment. Nutritionally complete food may constitute the sole source of nourishment or may be used as a partial replacement or supplement to the patient’s diet.The draft Requirements define the substances that may be used in the manufacture of food for special medical purposes and establish minimum and maximum levels of vitamins and minerals for products developed for infants and for products other than those developed for infants. They also set requirements concerning pesticide residues in products intended for infants and young children, and requirements for information on food, labelling, presentation and advertising.
items.eif: Three months from the date of official publication.

items.ko: 살생물제품법안 개정
items.orig: Draft Law of Ukraine "On Biocidal Products"
items.products: Biocidal products
items.desc: The draft Law of Ukraine “On Biocidal Products” is intended to regulate legal relations concerning the approval of active substances used in biocidal products, the state registration, production, making available on the market, placing on the market and safe use of biocidal products and treated articles. It also defines the rights and obligations of legal entities and individuals, as well as the powers of state authorities and their officials in the field of biocidal products.Specifically, the draft Law:designates an authorized state entity to conduct the assessment of materials concerning the approval, renewal or review of approval of active substances, prepare expert conclusions on the approval, renewal or review of approval of active substances, and prepare expert conclusions on the possibility of state registration of biocidal products under a simplified procedure;establishes the procedure and criteria for authorizing such entity, the duration of its authorization and the procedure for withdrawal of the authorization, as well as the procedure for determining the fees for the relevant services;establishes requirements for laboratories conducting laboratory testing of active substances for the preparation of active substance dossiers, including accreditation requirements;provides for the establishment of the State Register of Biocidal Products, which is to become operational on 1 January 2030, through the modernization of the existing State Register of Disinfectants. The draft Law also stipulates that all registrations of disinfectants that are valid as of the date of entry into force of this Law shall remain valid until their expiry.The classification of biocidal products is set out separately in an Annex to the draft Law.This draft Law was previously notified in 2025 under the title “On Making Available on the Market and Use of Biocidal Products”.The draft Law is also notified in accordance with the requirements of the TBT Agreement.
items.eif: This Law will enter into force on the day following the day of its publication and will be enacted on 1 January 2030.

items.ko: 천연광천수 분류기준 및 천연광천수·샘물 안전요건 명령안 개정
items.orig: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of the Criteria for Classifying Drinking Water as Natural Mineral Water and the Safety Requirements for Natural Mineral Waters and Spring Waters"
items.products: Waters, incl. natural or artificial mineral waters and aerated waters, not containing added sugar, other sweetening matter or flavoured; ice and snow (HS code(s): 2201)
items.desc: The draft Order provides for the approval of the Criteria for classifying drinking water as natural mineral water and the Safety Requirements for natural mineral waters and spring waters.The Criteria establish geological, hydrogeological, physical, chemical, physico-chemical and microbiological requirements for classifying drinking water as natural mineral water. These include requirements concerning underground origin, protection from contamination, microbiological safety, stability of composition, temperature and other essential characteristics within natural variations. They also specify the natural characteristics of the water, including mineral substances, trace elements or other constituents, and define the term “normal total microbial count”.The Criteria also establish maximum levels for certain naturally occurring constituents that may pose a risk to human health and provide for pharmacological, physiological and clinical studies where necessary.The Safety Requirements set out microbiological safety requirements for natural mineral waters and spring waters, including maximum levels for the total microbial count and requirements concerning the absence of parasites and pathogenic microorganisms. They also establish maximum permissible levels of naturally occurring constituents in natural mineral waters and maximum permissible levels of residues resulting from the treatment of natural mineral waters and spring waters with ozone-enriched air.

items.ko: 천연광천수·샘물 위생요건 개정 명령안
items.orig: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine "On Amendments to the Order of the Ministry for Development of Economy, Trade and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 741 of 12 April 2021" (concerning Hygienic Requirements for the production and circulation of natural mineral water and spring water)
items.products: Natural mineral water and spring water
items.note: 같은 명령안을 TBT로도 통보(G/TBT/N/UKR/409)
items.desc: The draft Order provides for amendments to the Hygienic Requirements for the Production and Circulation of Natural Mineral Waters and Spring Waters, approved by Order of the Ministry for Development of Economy, Trade and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 741 of 12 April 2021, notified in documents G/SPS/N/UKR/156 and G/SPS/N/UKR/156/Add.1.The draft Order establishes conditions for the treatment of natural mineral waters and spring waters with ozone-enriched air and activated alumina to ensure the safety of the treatment processes and prevent changes to the essential characteristics of the waters.It sets requirements for the use of ozone-enriched air for the removal of compounds of iron, manganese, sulphur and arsenic, and for the use of activated alumina for the removal of excess fluoride compounds, including requirements concerning its initialisation, regeneration and quality control.The draft Order also establishes requirements concerning the permissible margins of error and the accuracy of safety testing of treated natural mineral waters and spring waters, the application of appropriate production and hygiene practices and the monitoring of critical stages of the treatment process. It also establishes labelling requirements for treated waters indicating the adsorption method used.The draft Order has been developed based on the provisions of Commission Directive 2003/40/EC and Commission Regulation (EU) No 115/2010. The draft Order is also notified under the TBT Agreement.

items.orig: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine “On Amendments to the Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine No. 118 of 12 March 2019” (concerning the Requirements for the Safety and Quality of Milk and Dairy Products)
items.products: Milk and dairy products
items.note: 같은 명령안을 TBT로도 통보(G/TBT/N/UKR/413)
items.desc: The draft Order proposes amendments to Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine of 12 March 2019 No. 118 "On Approval of the Requirements for Safety and Quality of Milk and Dairy Products", in particular with regard to: establishing specific calendar dates for the mandatory application of criteria to raw milk, replacing the reference to the date of termination or cancellation of martial law, namely 1 January 2029 and 1 January 2028, respectively;adding a definition of the term “milk raw material” and clarifying the terminology in accordance with the legislation;extending the exemption for own consumption to the preparation, processing and storage of dairy products;introducing requirements for demonstrating the representativeness of raw milk samples with regard to fat and protein content, as well as criteria for sample unsuitability and the consequences of determining such unsuitability;supplementing the list of research (testing) methods with reference methods for determining fat and protein content and expanding the list of alternative analytical methods;clarifying the conditions for the use of milk and colostrum that do not meet the established requirements.The draft Order is aslo notified under the TBT Agreement as regards requirements for materials and articles intended to come into contact with milk and dairy products, as well as identification marking and related information requirements.
items.eif: This Order will enter into force on the day of its official publication.

items.ko: 밀가루 국가표준(SNI) 의무적용 산업부 규정 개정 — 2026년 제21호
items.orig: Mandatory Implementation of the Indonesian National Standard for Wheat Flour
items.products: Wheat flour for foodstuff
items.desc: Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 61 of 2024 has been revised by Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 21 of 2026 regarding Mandatory Implementation of Indonesia National Standard for Wheat Fluor for Food Use. The amendment revises the requirements for mandatory SNI certification of wheat flour for food use. Key changes include expanding the eligible business classification codes for repackers to KBLI 10616, 82920, and/or 82922; removing the requirement for repackers to maintain sieving facilities; and explicitly exempting repackers from testing equipment requirements. Domestic industrial companies may submit a declaration of implementation of ISO 9001:2015 and/or a food safety management system without the previous one-year business licensing restriction. The requirement to obtain the corresponding management system certificate by the second surveillance is also removed, while the trademark certificate requirement remains. Minimum audit durations are reduced to two person-days for repackers’ initial certification and recertification, and for domestic surveillance audits. The certification scheme is updated accordingly. SNI 3751:2018 and the Type 5 certification scheme remain unchanged. The amendment entered into force on 31 July 2026.

items.ko: 팜 식용유 국가표준(SNI) 의무적용 산업부 규정 개정 — 2026년 제14호
items.orig: Mandatory Implementation of the Indonesian National Standard for Palm Cooking Oil
items.desc: Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 3 of 2025 has been revised by Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 14 of 2026 regarding Mandatory Implementation of Indonesia National Standard for Palm Oil. The amendment revises the requirements for mandatory SNI certification of palm cooking oil, particularly for repackers. Key changes include expanding the eligible business classification codes for repackers to KBLI 10437, 82920, and/or 82922, and replacing the minimum facility requirement for filtration and packaging with storage and packaging facilities. The revised provisions require repackers to own a trademark in Class 29, including collective trademarks, and remove the previously stated alternative of holding a trademark licensing agreement. The certification scheme is revised to reflect these changes. SNI 7709:2019 and the Type 5 certification scheme remain unchanged. The amendment entered into force on 23 June 2026.

items.orig: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “On Amendments to Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 980 of 29 July 2026” (related to the labelling of food and feed)
items.products: Food products for special medical purposes and infant food, prepacked imported food products
items.desc: The revised draft Resolution proposes specific rules concerning the labelling and circulation of imported food products under Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 980 of 29 July 2026 "On Repealing Certain Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Concerning the Labelling of Food and Feed", in particular:during martial law, food products for special medical purposes and infant food imported to Ukraine as humanitarian aid, for which information is provided in a language other than the state language, may remain in circulation in Ukraine until the end of their minimum durability date or use-by date. The circulation of such food products is permitted exclusively to recipients and/or beneficiaries of humanitarian aid;until 1 April 2027, prepacked imported food products for which the mandatory information on the packaging or label is provided in a language other than the state language, may be imported to Ukraine, placed on the market and sold, provided that:consignments of prepacked imported food products are accompanied, at all stages of the food chain, by complete information on the food products, in accordance with the requirements of the Law of Ukraine "On Information for Consumers on Food Products", provided in the state language in paper and/or electronic form;a food market operator that sells prepacked imported food products to the final consumer provides the consumer, free of charge and before purchase, with access to the mandatory information on the food product in the state language by one of the following means, at the operator’s choice: displaying the information directly at the place where the food product is sold or next to it; displaying a QR code on the price tag or shelf, packaging, or another physical medium located directly next to the food product; using an electronic price tag, information terminal or another electronic device at the place where the food product is sold; displaying the information on the website or in the mobile application of the food market operator; providing the information in printed form or by another means that ensures the consumer has free access to such information;in the case of distance selling, the mandatory information on the food product in the state language, except for information on the minimum durability date or use-by date, is available to the consumer before the completion of the order, while the complete information is provided upon delivery.Prepacked imported food products ref

items.products: Alcoholic Beverages (HS Codes: 2203; 2204; 2205; 2206; 2208)
items.desc: The Draft Communiqué proposes changing the warning phrase "Alcohol is not your friend” found in Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Communiqué on Warning Messages to be Placed on Alcoholic Beverage Packaging (published in the Official Gazette dated 11 August 2013 and numbered 28732) to "Alcohol can cause cancer."Furthermore, the Draft Communiqué envisages updating the packaging and warning regulations (Article 3/1/d) which were previously notified to the WTO under G/TBT/N/TUR/41 and its subsequent addendum (G/TBT/N/TUR/41/Add.1 and G/TBT/N/TUR/41/Add.2) as well as modifying mandatory QR code placement requirements and the dimensions of warning messages.This Communiqué shall enter into force on the date of its publication.PROVISIONAL ARTICLE 1 – Except for products manufactured for export purposes, the production, importation, and placing on the domestic market by manufacturers and importers of products that do not meet the requirements set forth in Articles 2 and 3 of this Communiqué shall be prohibited as of six months after the date of entry into force of the Communiqué introducing this Article.

items.products: Products refer to food, beverages, drugs, and cosmetics that are produced or processed through processing services.
items.desc: The guidelines establish a reference for Business Actors for the implementation of the Halal Product Assurance System (SJPH) for Processing Services related to food, beverages, drugs, and cosmetics. The guidelines cover processing services, including contract manufacturing (maklon), shared kitchens, water processing, milling, and other processing services, and set requirements concerning halal commitment and responsibility, materials, Halal Product Processes (PPH), production facilities, packaging and labelling, traceability, internal audits, and management review. items.orig: Order of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 7417 "On Approval of the Requirements for Preserved Tuna and Bonito" of 9 July 2026
items.products: Preserved tuna and bonito
items.desc: The Order approves the Requirements for preserved tuna and bonito, which establish standards governing the placing on the market of preserved tuna (Thunnus) and bonito (Bonito) to ensure adequate consumer information and prevent business practices that mislead consumers.The Requirements establish conditions for the use of food names, specify the fish species that may be used for tuna and bonito, and prohibit the mixing of different fish species in one package unit, except in the case of products of culinary preparation containing a specified minimum content of tuna, bonito or their mixture. They also establish requirements for the forms of presentation of the products and for the liquid medium used in preserved products, including requirements for the corresponding designations in the name of the food product.The name of the food product must comply with the established requirements and, as applicable, include the fish species, the form of presentation and a description of the liquid medium. The simultaneous use of the names “tuna” and “bonito” in the name of the food product is prohibited. The Requirements also establish minimum fish content depending on the form of presentation and the liquid medium used.The Order provides that preserved tuna and bonito that comply with the legislation on food safety and certain quality parameters applicable before the entry into force of this Order, but do not comply with all or certain provisions of the Requirements for preserved tuna and bonito approved by this Order, may remain on the market until the expiry of their minimum durability date or use-by date.
items.eif: This Order will enter into force six months after the date of its official publication, i.e. on 15 March 2027.

items.orig: Public Health Protection (Food) (Iodized table salt enrichment), 5786 – 2026
items.products: Table salt (HS code(s): 2501); (ICS code(s): 67.040)
items.desc: Israeli research indicates a significant iodine deficiency among the Israeli population: approximately 60% of the child population suffers from iodine deficiency, and approximately 85% of pregnant women suffer from iodine deficiency, which may impair the normal development of the fetus. These data require structured, systematic state intervention to prevent and correct iodine deficiency through salt iodization, which is an effective, safe, and agreed-upon method implemented in over 120 countries worldwide.These new regulations prohibit the production or sale of table salt unless an iodine compound has been added, so the iodine content must be between 25 mg and 45 mg per kilogram of salt. It also defines terms, sets labeling requirements, and establishes a mechanism for monitoring implementation.The regulations will enter into force 12 months after publication in Israel's Official Gazette. This period is intended to allow the Israeli salt industry and importers to prepare for implementing the new requirements.
items.eif: The regulations will enter into force 12 months after publication in Israel's Official Gazette. This period is intended to allow the Israeli salt industry and importers to prepare for the new requirements.

items.products: Poultry meat, eggs and their products
items.desc: Following the WOAH report dated 1 September 2026, a Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) virus outbreak has occurred in Maine-et-Loire in France. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.4, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Maine-et-Loire in France to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the HPAI virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in France prove that the product is free from the virus).

items.orig: Draft Circular of the Minister of Agriculture and Environment on Management of Livestock Breeds and Livestock Breed Products
items.products: Live animals and animal genetic material covered by the Draft Circular, including breeding animals, hatching eggs, semen, embryos and other genetic material of livestock breeds, in particular breeds listed in the List of livestock breeds requiring conservation and the List of livestock breeds prohibited from export (HS codes: 0101-0106, 0407, 0511.10 and 0511.99; ICS code: 65.020.30)
items.desc: The Draft Circular consolidates and updates Viet Nam's rules on the management of livestock breeds and livestock breed products. It covers the international exchange of rare and precious animal genetic resources; the export or international exchange of livestock breeds and livestock breed products included in the List of livestock breeds prohibited from export; the List of livestock breeds requiring conservation; and the List of livestock breeds prohibited from export.It also prescribes requirements and procedures for testing and recognition of testing results for livestock lines and breeds; recognition of new livestock lines and breeds; minimum quality levels for livestock breeds; and certificates of training in artificial insemination and embryo transfer techniques. Applications may be submitted in person, by post or electronically, with specified processing time limits and responsibilities for updating the national livestock database.The Draft Circular maintains and standardizes four administrative procedures, clarifies central and provincial competence, reduces or simplifies processing requirements, and strengthens traceability, electronic processing and post-market control. It does not maintain the former procedure for registration of breed testing or the former procedure for first-time import of breeding males, semen and embryos; importers remain responsible for origin, declared standards and quality under applicable legislation.The Draft Circular will replace Circular No. 22/2019/TT-BNNPTNT dated 30 November 2019 and Circular No. 21/2024/TT-BNNPTNT dated 11 December 2024 and repeal the relevant provisions and forms of Circular No. 94/2025/TT-BNNMT dated 31 December 2025, Circular No. 22/2026/TT-BNNMT dated 19 May 2026 and Circular No. 23/2019/TT-BNNPTNT dated 30 November 2019. Transitional provisions preserve the validity of approvals, decisions and certificates already issued and provide for continued processing of applications received before entry into force.
items.eif: To be determined.

items.products: processed animal protein feed derived from poultry (poultry by product meal, feather meal etc.,)
items.desc: Additional provisions have been added to the draft amendment notified in G/SPS/N/KOR/844 (9 April 2026). The main content of the draft amendment is to allow poultry-derived products produced in countries from which imports into the Republic of Korea are prohibited to be imported into the Republic of Korea, in accordance with the prescribed procedures, provided that they have been rendered. The newly added provisions specify that, during the rendering process, the products must be treated either with moist heat at a minimum temperature of 56 °C for 30 minutes, or by heating the entire product to a minimum internal temperature of 74 °C, or by a method demonstrated to have an equivalent or greater efficacy. This measure has been established to ensure a minimum level of safety against highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in the importation of poultry-derived products, taking into consideration the treatment conditions recommended in Article 10.4.19 of the WOAH Terrestrial Animal Health Code for the importation of poultry-derived products intended for use as animal feed.

items.desc: The Draft Order establishes the Protective Measures for some animal origin products intended for animal consumption and imported from Ukraine transposing into national legislation the provisions of Directive (EC) 2002/805, including the restrictive measure: of a temporary interdiction or a special authorization regime on import of powdered milk and powdered formula obtained from powdered milk for animal feed, originating from Ukraine; and the obligation of sampling to detect the presence of chloramphenicol for every batch of this type, before market placement. The act aims to protect animal health, ensure a rigorous mechanism for verification of conformities, harmonize the legal framework with European standards, and facilitate international trade.

items.orig: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine “On Approval of the Requirements for Good Distribution Practice of Veterinary Medicinal Products”
items.products: Veterinary medicinal products
items.desc: The draft Order provides for the approval of the Requirements for Good Distribution Practice of Veterinary Medicinal Products. These Requirements are mandatory for veterinary medicinal product market operators holding a licence to carry out activities involving the manufacture and import of veterinary medicinal products and their wholesale distribution, as well as for veterinary medicinal product market operators holding a licence to carry out wholesale distribution of veterinary medicinal products, including those operating under special customs regimes, such as free zones or customs warehouses. The draft Order establishes Good Distribution Practice requirements for veterinary medicinal products regarding: quality management, including the quality system; personnel, including personnel training; premises, equipment, computerized systems, qualification of equipment and validation of processes; documentation, procedures and record-keeping; operations, including the approval of suppliers and customers, requirements for the receipt and storage of veterinary medicinal products, the destruction of unsuitable veterinary medicinal products, order picking, supply and export; handling of complaints, returned and falsified veterinary medicinal products, and the recall of veterinary medicinal products from the market; activities of third-party contractors; self-inspections; transportation of veterinary medicinal products, including those requiring special transportation conditions.
items.eif: This Order will enter into force six months after the date of its official publication, except for paragraph 2 of Subsection 2 of Section IV (concerning temperature mapping and temperature monitoring), which will enter into force on 1 October 2028.

items.desc: It was announced that the revised Plant Quarantine Regulation was published on 6 May 2026, and the SPS notification was published with the symbol G/SPS/N/TUR/23/Rev.1/Add.2. In addition, the English text of the Plant Quarantine Regulation, which was published on 6 May 2026 and entered into force on 4 August 2026, was announced with the symbol G/SPS/N/TUR/23/Rev.1/Add.4, along with the SPS notification. With the entry into force of the Regulation on 4 August 2026, paragraph 13 of Article 8 of the Regulation was titled "Import Control" and The provision states that:“For plants and plant products listed in Annex-4 for which pest-free area information relating to the production site is required, the list of areas designated as free from the relevant pest by the national plant protection organisation in the country of origin is notified in advance in accordance with the relevant ISPMs. In the event of a change in the phytosanitary status of the areas reported as free from the pest, the national plant protection organization shall submit an updated list of such areas.”In this context, for the import of plants and plant products listed in Annex 4 for which information on pest-free areas related to the production area is required, the list of areas determined by the country of origin’s National Plant Protection Organization to be free from the relevant pest must be officially notified in advance to our country’s National Plant Protection Organization.Official controls of the relevant shipments will not be initiated until the said free area lists are officially notified to our country by the National Plant Protection Organization of the country of origin. As stated in subparagraph (b) of paragraph 1 of Article 16 of the Regulation, 20 days are given to complete the deficiencies in the documents. If the deficiencies cannot be completed within this period, the procedures for the return of the shipments to the exporting country will be initiated.

items.orig: Circular amending, supplementing a number of articles of various circulars in the field of agriculture and environment
items.products: Pesticides, fertilizers, plant varieties (HS codes: 31.01, 31.02, 31.03, 31.04, 31.05, 38.08)
items.desc: The draft Circular amends, supplements or abolish a number of regulations in the field of agriculture and environment: - Plant production and protection: (i) decentralize from the Minister of Agriculture and Environment to the Chair persons of provincial-level People’s Committee in dealing with administrative procedures for the State inspection of imported pesticide quality; (ii) abolish the conditions for granting Decision on recognition of plant variety testing bodies, and abolish administrative procedures for granting, re-granting the Decision on recognition of plant variety testing bodies; (iii) abolish administrative procedures for self-declaration of plant variety circulation; (iv) extend valid duration of Decision on recognition of fertilizer circulation in Viet Nam from five years to ten years; (v) simplify administrative procedures for granting Pesticide import License.- Fisheries: abolish Article 5 of Circular 16/2026/TT-BNNMT to have consistence with the relevant regulations of the revised Law on Fisheries.- Dyke management: revise scope of application in the light that guidance is only provided to consult with the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment on acceptance of dyke-related activities.The draft Circular aims to promptly implement relevant higher-level legal instruments; reduce and simplify administrative procedures and business investment conditions; promote decentralization; update procedures and forms; reduce processing time and compliance costs; and facilitate production, business and trade activities by organizations and individuals.

items.desc: The draft Decree amends, supplements or abolish a number of regulations in the field of plant production and protection:(i) abolish administrative procedures for re-granting Pesticide import License; (ii) abolish fertilizer business conditions, administrative procedures for the State management of imported fertilizer inspection, administrative procedures for re-granting fertilizer manufacturing eligibility certificates when such certificates are lost or damaged;(iii) abolish conditions for granting Decision on recognition of a plant variety testing body, and administrative procedures for granting, re-granting Decision on recognition of a plant variety testing body; (iv) decentralize from the Minister of Agriculture and Environment to the Chair persons of provincial-level People’s Committee in dealing with two administrative procedures for certifying and re-certifying the export fragrant rice which enjoys tax-free import quotas; (v) abolish conditions for re-issuing representative service Certificates for plant variety right;(vi) reduce time to carry out some administrative procedures. At the same time, this draft Decree regulates a transition provision related to plant variety testing. The draft Decree aims to reduce, simplify administrative procedures, business investment conditions, decentralization; update processes and forms.

note.lead: 10월 식품 관련 통보 164건에서 눈여겨볼 흐름은 네 가지입니다.

themes.title: 농약 잔류허용기준 통보가 여러 나라에서 나왔습니다
themes.text: 일본이 티아디닐·펜아자퀸·1,3-디클로로프로펜 잔류허용기준 개정안을, 캐나다가 플루디옥소닐·사이프로디닐 기준안을, 뉴질랜드가 농업용 화합물 잔류허용기준 개정안을 통보했습니다. 유럽연합은 디페노코나졸 기준을 확정하고, 트리클로피르·펜메디팜 재승인을 거부하는 안을 TBT로 냈습니다. 재승인 거부는 잔류허용기준 조정으로 이어질 수 있습니다.

themes.title: 걸프 7개국이 식품 기술규정 9건을 묶어 통보했습니다
themes.text: 걸프 7개국이 식품·사료 중 오염물질·독소 최대기준 추가통보와 함께 카다멈·캐슈너트·사프란·딸기·과일채소 절임·아티초크 통조림·빵가루 입힌 냉동 수산물 규격, 화학농약 요건을 통보했습니다. 같은 규격 대부분을 TBT로도 냈습니다.

themes.title: 오염물질·가공 관련 기준이 새로 나왔습니다
themes.text: 마카오는 식품 중 중금속 최대기준 165개 가운데 92개를 신설·조정했습니다. 우크라이나는 식품 중 아크릴아마이드 저감 요건, 비상 시 식품·사료 방사능 최대허용수준, 식품 제조용 추출용매 요건을 통보했습니다. 브라질은 식품접촉용 셀룰로오스 재질 규정 재검토안을 냈습니다.

themes.title: 가축질병을 이유로 한 수입 금지가 늘었습니다
themes.text: 필리핀이 구제역 감수성 동물 유래 품목과 영국산 소·쇠고기 수입을 일시 금지했고, 영국은 구제역 유입 방지 특별조치를 통보했습니다. 사우디아라비아는 뉴캐슬병을 이유로 폴란드 마워폴스카·비엘코폴스카주와 브라질 산타카타리나주산 가금 수입을 금지했습니다. 에콰도르는 아프리카돼지열병 방역조치를 냈고, 콜롬비아는 아르헨티나산 가금 관련 수입 중단을 풀었습니다.

items.ko: EU 식품첨가물 규격(규정 231/2012) 개정사항 국내 적용 공중보건 고시 개정
items.orig: Public Health Protection Notice (Food) (Application of Changes to the Annex to European Union Directives) (Regulation 231/2012 - Specifications of Food Additives Listed in Annexes II and III to Regulation No. 1333/2008), 5786-2026
items.products: Food additives (ICS code(s): 67.220.20)
items.desc: Commission Regulation (EU) No. 231/2012 of 9 March 2012 determines specifications for food additives listed in Annexes II and III to Regulation No. 1333/2008 of the European Commission and of the Council (hereinafter - Regulation 231/2012) was adopted in Israel as part of Amendment No. 10 to the Public Health Protection (Food) Law, 5776-2015 (hereinafter - the Law/Food Law), and appears in Item 9 of Appendix II A to the Law. Regulation 231/2012 was fully implemented, with the expansion listed in Column C of Item 9 of Appendix II A to the Law, in addition to the exceptions as stated in Section 3A(a1) to (a5) of the Law.To date, notices have been published in the Official Gazette (Reshumot) that included changes that took place in the European Union in Regulation 231/2012, and were applied in Israel (updates), with the most recent being published on 21 April 2026, being the Public Health Protection Notice (Food) (Application of Changes to the Annex to the European Union Directives) (Regulation 231/2012 - Specifications of Food Additives Listed in Annexes II and III to Regulation No. 1333/2008) (No. 2)(Amendment), 5786-2026, signed by the Director of the National Food Service in the Ministry of Health, as she was then described. The latest updated consolidated version, adopted and published on the Food Service website after the publication of the aforementioned notice, is the version valid in European legislation as it stood on 27 October 2025.It is now proposed to apply in Israel the changes to the Annex to Regulation 231/2012 that will be applied in the European Union, without modifications, conditions, exceptions, or expansions, while integrating them into the text of Regulation 231/2012 as adopted today. The essence of the changes is in the specifications of food additives. It is clarified that the expansion that appears in column C of item 9 in Appendix II A will continue to apply to the changes proposed to be implemented in Israel. The changes included in this proposed amendment combine the following EU Regulations amending various Annexes of Regulation (EC) No. 231/2012: 1. COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2024/2597 of 4 October 2024 amending Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the use of sorbic acid (E 200) and potassium sorbate (E 202) and the Annex to Commission Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 as regards the specifications for sorbic acid (E 200), potassium sorbate (E 202) and propyl gallate (E 310
items.eif: 1(a) and 2(a) - 20 May 2025; a(b), 2(b) and 3 - 1 November 2025 25 August 2025 27 December 2025 1 July 2026 18 October 2026 18 October 2026

items.desc: The Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Flavourings and Certain Food Ingredients with Flavouring Properties for Use in And on Foods, which was notified through G/SPS/N/TUR/151 (22 November 2024), was adopted and published in the Official Gazette dated 14 September 2026 and numbered 33370. The Regulation establishes provisions on food flavourings, food ingredients with flavouring properties, the source materials used in their production, their conditions of use and labelling principles, as well as production conditions for smoke flavourings. The Regulation entered into force on the date of its publication. Food business operators subject to the Regulation must comply with its provisions by 31 December 2026. Products placed on the market before 31 December 2026 may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life in accordance with the transitional provisions. Certain flavouring substances listed in the transitional provision may no longer be placed on the market, used in food production or imported as of 31 December 2026.

items.orig: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of the State Medical and Sanitary Standards for Maximum Permitted Levels of Radioactive Contamination of Food and Feed”
items.products: food and feed
items.desc: The draft Order proposes to approve the State Medical and Sanitary Standards for Maximum Permitted Levels of Radioactive Contamination of Food and Feed following a nuclear or radiological emergency. The draft Order establishes maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed, including contamination by strontium-90, iodine-131, caesium-134, caesium-137, plutonium-239 and americium-241 (Sr-90, I-131, Cs-134, Cs-137, Pu-239 and Am-241), and provides that the Standards shall apply for three months from the date of occurrence and/or receipt, in accordance with the procedure established by law, of notification of a nuclear or radiological emergency. The Standards shall apply to food, beverages, including alcoholic beverages, and feed that have been or may be radioactively contaminated in the event of a nuclear or radiological emergency and that are produced and/or placed on the market in Ukraine, or imported (consigned) into the customs territory of Ukraine from the country of origin or consignment following such an emergency. It is also established that the State Hygienic Standards “Permitted Levels of Radionuclide Content of ^137Cs and ^90Sr in Food and Drinking Water”, approved by Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 256 of 3 May 2006, shall not apply where and to the extent that the maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination established by the Standards approved by this Order are applicable in accordance with the legislation. The established maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed, including food and feed placed on the market, will contribute to protecting the population from the adverse effects of ionising radiation associated with the consumption of radioactively contaminated food and, indirectly, with the consumption by animals of radioactively contaminated feed resulting from a nuclear or radiological emergency.
items.eif: This Order will enter into force from the day of its official publication.

items.products: Extraction solvents used in the production of foodstuffs and food ingredients
items.desc: The draft Order has been developed with the aim of establishing requirements for extraction solvents permitted for use in the production of foodstuffs and food ingredients. The Requirements establish a list of extraction solvents permitted for use in the production of foodstuffs and food ingredients, the conditions of their use, maximum residue limits for extraction solvents in foodstuffs and food ingredients as well as general and specific purity criteria for such solvents. These Requirements also apply to imported foodstuffs and food ingredients that have been produced using extraction solvents. The draft Order also establishes that foodstuffs and food ingredients that complied with the requirements of the legislation on the safety and certain quality parameters of foodstuffs in force before the entry into force of this Order, but do not comply with the Requirements for Extraction Solvents Used in the Production of Foodstuffs and Food Ingredients approved by this Order, may be imported into the customs territory of Ukraine, produced and/or placed on the market for three years following the entry into force of this Order. Such foodstuffs may remain on the market until the expiry of their minimum durability date or “use by” date.

items.orig: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine “On Approval of the Hygienic Requirements for Reducing Acrylamide Levels in Food”
items.products: french fries, other cut (deep fried) products and sliced potato crisps from fresh potatoes; potato crisps, snacks, crackers and other potato products from potato dough; bread; breakfast cereals (excluding porridge); fine bakery wares, including biscuits, cookies, rusks, cereal bars, rolls, wafers, gingerbread, crackers and crispbread; roast and instant coffee; coffee substitutes; baby food and pro
items.desc: The draft Order provides for the approval of the Hygienic Requirements for Reducing Acrylamide Levels in Food.The Requirements specify the food products to which mitigation measures to reduce the presence of acrylamide apply, establish the relevant mitigation measures for food business operators and set benchmark levels for acrylamide to verify the effectiveness of those measures.The Requirements provide for differentiated mitigation measures for food business operators producing and placing the relevant food products on the market, including producers, retail operators and chain establishments. They also establish requirements for establishing programmes for own sampling and analysis, keeping records of the mitigation measures applied and the results of sampling and analysis, determining sampling frequency, and reviewing mitigation measures in light of the results obtained.Food business operators producing and placing food products on the market shall apply appropriate mitigation measures to achieve levels of acrylamide as low as reasonably achievable and below the benchmark levels for acrylamide in food set out in Annex 1 to the Requirements.The benchmark levels serve as indicators for verifying the effectiveness of the mitigation measures implemented by food business operators to ensure compliance with food hygiene requirements at all stages of production and distribution, within the framework of procedures based on the principles of the Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) system.

items.desc: This regulation provides clarifications on the hierarchy of food safety standards that have already been established and adopted as technical regulations, serving as points of reference for government agencies, international trading partners and local stakeholders. The scope of this regulation does not cover any requirements for compliance with regulatory procedures, issuances, or laboratory analyses, or any other substantial compliance costs to the stakeholders nor the government agencies. Tailored to meet the specific needs of Food Business Operators (FBOs), it serves as a clear reference point for determining the applicable food safety standards. The regulation offers alternatives for the regulatory agencies and the FBOs in cases of unavailability of PNS and Codex standards to cater the needs of the stakeholders while ensuring the safety of the plant foods.

items.orig: Administrative Regulation No. 27/2026 Amendment to Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food"
items.products: Food
items.desc: To further safeguard public health, enhance the efficiency of risk management, and promote harmonization between local regulations and international standards, the Macao Special Administrative Region Government has amended Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food". This amendment is based on the latest standards recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC), as well as those established by major food-supplying countries and regions. This regulation has been scrutinized through risk assessment to ensure that it adequately protect public health in Macao, China.The revised regulation establishes a total of 165 maximum limits (MLs) for specified heavy metal contaminants in specific food items, of which 92 MLs represent optimizations or new additions. A reasonable transition period of approximately 6 months will be granted following the official promulgation of the regulation. This will provide sufficient time for the food industry to adapt its importation and safety control processes, and for local testing laboratories to establish and validate the necessary analytical capabilities in accordance with the new requirements.

items.desc: This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk" (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.c. Amend the name designations of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk" to align with the raw materials used.

items.products: Food additives
items.desc: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/SPS/N/TUR/126 on 20/06/2022. The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: 13 October 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonized with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.• The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.• E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.• For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.• E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.• E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.• The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabilizers) in some tradit

items.ko: 수입 할랄제품 적합성 검증 규정 공포 — BPJPH 2026년 제4호
items.orig: Regulation of The Halal Product Assurance Organizing Agency of The Republic of Indonesia Number 4 of 2026 Concerning Conformity Verification of Foreign Halal Products Entering The Territory of Indonesia
items.products: This regulation applies to all goods and services subject to the phased implementation of mandatory halal certification under Government Regulation No. 42 of 2024 concerning the Implementation of Halal Product Assurance, including food, beverages, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, chemical products, biological products, genetically engineered products, consumer goods used, utilized or consumed by the pu
items.desc: This Regulation establishes the requirements and procedures for verifying the conformity of imported products with Indonesia’s halal product assurance requirements. Verification comprises administrative document checks and limited physical conformity inspections conducted by inspection bodies designated by BPJPH at the loading warehouse in the country of loading and/or origin prior to shipment. These activities cover conformity with halal certificates or foreign halal certificate registration numbers, halal labelling or non-halal information requirements, import documentation, and other applicable halal product assurance requirements. The results are documented in a Halal Product Verification Report (LPPH), which is valid for a single shipment or importation and is required upon submission of the import customs declaration. The Regulation further stipulates requirements for the designation of inspection bodies, application procedures, fees, exemptions for specified categories of goods, reporting obligations, monitoring and evaluation, and administrative sanctions. It shall enter into force 30 days after the date of promulgation.

Tank vehicle. Sanitary and technical requirements. The description of content of the notified Technical Standard stated that it establishes the sanitary and technical requirements to be met by tank vehicles that are used for transporting and distributing water for human consumption, and the technical, administrative and legal provisions to be met by natural or legal persons engaged in that activity. Natural or legal persons, whether public or private, who transport and distribute water for human consumption using tank vehicles must comply with the notified standard. It applies to regular and irregular supply scenarios and service interruptions, including scheduled interruptions and emergency interruptions caused by natural or anthropogenic phenomena. items.products: Organic products
items.desc: The draft Resolution establishes Detailed Rules for the organic production and circulation of organic products and in-conversion products. The Rules set out requirements for various categories of organic production, including plant production, livestock production, aquaculture and the production of processed organic products.The Rules lay down requirements for production methods, the use of products and substances permitted in organic production, the prevention of contamination and mixing with non-organic products, traceability, record-keeping and documentation required for certification. They also establish requirements for labelling, packaging, storage and transport of organic products, as well as specific requirements applicable to different categories of products.The draft Resolution provides for a transitional period until 1 January 2030 for market operators whose facilities require reconstruction and/or whose land areas need to be expanded to comply with certain production requirements.
items.eif: This Resolution will enter into force simultaneously with the Law of Ukraine No. 4921-IX of 30 June 2026 “On State Regulation of Organic Production, Circulation and Labeling of Organic Products”, i.e. on 21 July 2029.

items.orig: Proposal P1067 – Health Star Rating System: 2nd Call for Submissions and Supporting Documents.
items.products: Imported and domestically produced packaged foods for retail sale in Australia and New Zealand that are required to bear a label, subject to certain exemptions and prohibitions.
items.desc: FSANZ has prepared a proposed draft amendment to the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (the Code) to mandate the display of a Health Star Rating (HSR) symbol on food for sale in Australia and New Zealand. The 2nd call for submissions provides FSANZ’s assessment and the proposed draft amendment, which would require the HSR to be calculated using a prescribed algorithm and the HSR symbol to be displayed on the front of most packaged foods for retail sale that are required to bear a nutrition information panel, subject to specified exemptions and prohibitions. FSANZ seeks submissions on the proposed regulatory approach to inform its final assessment and a decision on whether to approve, amend or reject the proposed draft amendment.
items.adopt: Notification to Australian and New Zealand Government anticipated May 2027 with adoption (gazettal) to follow shortly after, pending Government consideration.
items.eif: A three-year transition period has been proposed beginning on the date of gazettal, with a further two-year stock-in-trade period.

items.products: Preparations of a kind used in animal feeding (HS code(s): 2309)
items.desc: Two anise tinctures and anise essential oil from Pimpinella anisum L. were initially authorised in accordance with Directive 70/524/EEC as feed additives for all animal species in the category of ‘sensory additives’ and in the functional group ‘flavouring compounds’. Applications were later submitted for the reauthorisation of these substances in accordance with article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003. Based on the conclusions of the scientific assessments of the dossiers submitted by the applicants, conducted by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), it is proposed to reauthorise these substances as feed additives for certain animal species in the additive category of ‘sensory additives’ and in the functional group ‘flavouring compounds’, under certain conditions detailed in the Annex to the draft Act. In addition, the proposed measure aims to withdraw the placing on the market of these substances in respect of the animal species and categories other than those mentioned in the Annex. Transitional periods are laid down for the interested parties to prepare themselves to meet the requirement concerning the new authorisation of the concerned substances and their withdrawal from the market in respect of the animal species and categories other than those mentioned in the Annex.
items.eif: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

items.orig: Resolución Ejecutiva No.046-2026 Regulación de ciertas sustancias de uso veterinario prohibidas y restringidas en la Republica de Nicaragua (Executive Resolution No. 046-2026 regulating certain prohibited and restricted substances for veterinary use in the Republic of Nicaragua)
items.products: Substances for veterinary use
items.desc: The notified Executive Resolution establishes provisions for regulating and controlling the use and marketing of substances for veterinary use, based on on their prohibited or restricted status.It prohibits, within the national territory, the manufacture, health registration, importation, sale, marketing, transport, storage, handling, possession, and use in all aquatic and terrestrial animal species, whether individually, in combination, as raw materials, in finished veterinary medicines, or as ingredient in animal feed, of the 56 substances listed in the second operative paragraph of Executive Resolution No. 046-2026;. It also sets out specific restrictions on clenbuterol, methyl violet, nitroimidazoles, avermectins, sulfonamides (sulfa drugs), antimicrobial growth promoters or performance enhancers, methylene blue, and chlorpromazine; and includes additional provisions for farms under the Segregated Bovine Production System (SSPB), and animals and products for export.
items.eif: 13 August 2026

items.products: Live swine, meat and products of swine
items.desc: The notified Executive Resolution lays down mandatory administrative, technical and health provisions concerning the registration, identification and traceability of swine in Nicaragua. These provisions are mandatory for any natural or legal person, whether public or private, involved in the swine supply chain. This includes:• Pig farms (industrial, semi-industrial, family-run or backyard)• Collection centres• Genetic centres• Transporters and means of transport of swine• Marketers• Slaughterhouses, municipal abattoirs, and processing plants.The Resolution provides for registration in the Trazar-Agro traceability system and assignment of a Unique Facility Identifier (CUE); it also regulates individual or batch identification, including RFID ear tags for breeding stock and imported or exported swine.G/SPS/N/NIC/377- 2 -

items.orig: The Law on Fisheries
items.products: Aquatic plants, aquatic animals, products of aquatic plants, aquatic animalsand other regulated articles
items.desc: The Law on Fisheries promulgated on 28 June 2025 comprises 104 articles and divided into 15 chapters. This law defines the management, conservation, and development of efficient and sustainable fisheries, aiming to promote food security and the national economy, as well as ensuring the protection of the rights and benefits of fishers, community fisheries, aquaculture farmers, and fish and fishery products business owners. The law also focuses on food safety, facilitating trade and transit of fish and fisheries products. Additionally, it aims to contribute to socio-economic development, welfare promotion and public health while ensuring the sustainability of natural resources and fisheries-ecological system in Cambodia. This law reflects Cambodia's high commitment in harmonizing its food safety regulations to the International Standards.

items.products: ICS code: 67.120
items.desc: The Circular institutes emergency measures for the importation of FMD-susceptible animals, their products and by-products originating from the specified countries. It bans the importation of FMD-susceptible animals, their products and by-products. It also sets conditions for commodities that remain allowed under the temporary restrictions, consistent with the Philippines’ import terms and conditions and regulatory requirements. The Circular further provides that non-compliant shipments shall be dealt with under DA Department Circular No. 14, Series of 2025, and that Veterinary Quarantine Officers/Inspectors shall stop and confiscate shipments of commodities classified as “NOT ALLOWED” at major ports of entry.

items.orig: Department Circular No. 50, Series of 2026: Temporary Ban on the Importation of Live Cattle, Meat, and Meat Products, and Bovine Processed Animal Proteins Derived from Cattle Originating from the United Kingdom
items.desc: The Circular institutes emergency measures concerning the importation of live cattle, skeletal meat and meat products, and bovine processed animal proteins originating from the United Kingdom. It temporarily bans the importation of these commodities; immediately suspends the processing, evaluation, and issuance of SPS import clearances for the commodities; and automatically revokes previously issued and approved SPS import clearances for shipments that have not arrived at Philippine ports. Shipments in transit, loaded, or accepted at the port of origin on or before the effectivity of the Circular may enter provided that live cattle were slaughtered, or products were manufactured, on or before 5 August 2026. Non-compliant shipments may be confiscated, re-exported, or destroyed at the importer/consignee’s expense. The Circular also requires more rigorous inspection of arrivals of meat and meat by-products derived from cattle, including live animals and bovine processed animal proteins.

items.products: Poultry meat, eggs and their products
items.desc: Following the WOAH report dated 1 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Małopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Małopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

items.desc: Following the WOAH report dated 19 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Wielkopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Wielkopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

The measures prohibit the import of hay and straw and certain animal by-products from animals susceptible to foot-and-mouth disease from any countries, or zones within countries, that are not recognised by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) as free of foot-and-mouth disease – either with or without vaccination. items.ko: 식물·식물산물 수입 시 훈증·소독 절차
items.orig: Fumigation and Disinfection Procedures for the Importation of Plants, Plant Products, and Other Substances
items.products: Plant and Plant Products Subjected to Phytosanitary Certificates
items.desc: During the import of plants, plant products and other substances to Türkiye; The Phytosanitary Certificate - issued by the official plant protection service of the exporting country addressed to Türkiye and in accordance with the ISPM 12 (International Phytosanitary Measures-Phytosanitary Certificates) standard must accompany the product. Information regarding the treatment carried out in the exporting country must be clearly stated in the "Disinfestation and/or Disinfection Treatment" section of the Phytosanitary Certificates.Where fumigation is carried out by the exporting country, whether at the request of the importing country (Türkiye) or otherwise, all treatments applied shall be fully specified in the relevant section(s) of the Phytosanitary Certificate (Disinfection and/or Disinfestation Treatment Section). Fumigation is an important pest control method for plants, plant products, and other materials, particularly in terms of controlling pests, reducing product losses, and meeting quarantine requirements. The Regulation on Plant Quarantine stipulates that fumigation must be carried out by the exporting country for certain products. However, even when fumigation is not required under the Regulation on Plant Quarantine, it is known that, in some cases, exporting countries fumigate consignments to mitigate the risk of products being exposed to contamination by harmful organisms during transportation. Because the plant protection products used for fumigation are toxic, they pose significant risks to living organisms, food safety, and the environment. In order to prevent such high risks and potential adverse consequences, the details of the fumigation treatment must be fully declared on the certificate for all consignments that have undergone fumigation, and the relevant fumigation documents must accompany the Phytosanitary Certificate.Furthermore, according to ISPM-12, the specified treatments must be those that are acceptable to the importing country and that are carried out or initiated in the exporting country under the supervision or authority of the exporting country’s National Plant Protection Organization (NPPO) to meet the phytosanitary import requirements.

items.orig: Proposed Rule: Cut Flowers Regulations; Removal of Chrysanthemum White Rust-Related Provisions
items.products: Cut flowers
items.desc: APHIS is amending the regulations governing the importation of fresh cut flowers to remove requirements for the importation of specific types of cut flowers from the regulations, and to list them in the U.S. Department of Agriculture database called the Agricultural Commodity Import Requirements instead. We are also removing entirely any restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers of the genera Chrysanthemum, Leucanthemella, and Nipponanthemum from countries in which chrysanthemum white rust ( Puccinia horiana P. Henn., CWR) is known to exist. This rule will allow us to use a notice-based, streamlined approach to update the import requirements for cut flowers and remove CWR-specific restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers.

items.products: Plants, plant products and other objects (HS chapters: 06 (live plants), 07 (vegetables), 08 (fruits), 09 (Spices), 12 (seeds), 14 (vegetable products), 44 (wood), 84 (machinery), 87 (vehicles), 94 (prefabricated buildings of wood))
items.desc: Implementing Regulation 2019/2072 contains the list of Union quarantine pests, protected zone quarantine pests, and regulated non-quarantine pests (RNQPs). Furthermore, it lays down phytosanitary requirements for import and internal movement of plants, plant products and other objects that may pose a phytosanitary risk to the European Union.This draft amendment of Implementing Regulation 2019/2072:Delists Aleurocanthus spiniferus, Raspberry leaf curl virus, and Strawberry leaf curl virus as quarantine pests and repeals measures associated with these pests.Lists the following species as quarantine pests and sets, where applicable, measures to avoid their entry and spread in the Union territory: Chloridea virescens, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4, Spodoptera ornithogalli, Spodoptera praefica, and Xanthomonas citri pv. viticolaPlease note that Chloridea virescens and Spodoptera ornithogalli were already listed in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1941 as species that are not to be introduced into, moved within, held, multiplied or released in the Union territory.Updates requirements for import and internal movement, including addition/revision of the respective CN codes, for Agrilus planipennis, Hirschmanniella spp., Meloidogyne enterolobii, and Thaumatotibia leucotretaLists Toumeyella parvicornis as regulated non-quarantine pest and sets measure to avoid its spread in the Union.Introduces changes to the protected zones in relation to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus and Erwinia amylovora.Clarifies and corrects some inconsistencies (e.g. change of scientific names).
items.eif: Entry into force 20 days after publication.

note.headline: 농약·중금속 기준 개정이 이어진 한 주
note.subtitle: 2026년 10월 26일~11월 1일 배포분 · 식품 관련 통보 47건
note.lead: 이번 주 식품 관련 통보 47건에서 눈여겨볼 흐름은 네 가지입니다.

themes.title: 농약·중금속 기준 개정이 이어졌습니다
themes.text: 일본이 티아디닐·펜아자퀸·1,3-디클로로프로펜 잔류허용기준 개정안 3건을, 호주가 생강 중 시아조파미드 기준 조정안을 통보했습니다. 마카오는 식품 중 중금속 최대기준 165개 가운데 92개를 신설·조정했고, 유럽연합은 펜메디팜 재승인 거부안을 내면서 잔류허용기준은 별도로 통보하겠다고 밝혔습니다.

themes.title: 가금 수입 제한이 잇따라 바뀌었습니다
themes.text: 사우디아라비아가 뉴캐슬병을 이유로 폴란드 비엘코폴스카주와 브라질 산타카타리나주산 가금육·계란 수입을 일시 금지했습니다. 같은 내용의 걸프 7개국 공동 통보는 잘못 배포돼 무효 처리됐습니다. 태국은 네덜란드산 가금 수입·경유 중단을 해제했습니다.

themes.title: 세 나라에서 표시 규정 통보가 나왔습니다
themes.text: 미국 텍사스주는 새우 원산지 표시 규칙안을, 호주는 건강별점 표시 의무화 제안의 2차 의견수렴을, 태국은 우유·가향우유 제품명 표시 개정안을 통보했습니다. 텍사스주 건은 의견 제출 기한이 11월 9일입니다.

themes.title: 우리나라도 검역병해충을 추가했습니다
themes.text: 농림축산검역본부가 검역병해충 36종 추가를 통보했습니다. 의견 제출 기한은 12월 27일입니다.

items.ko: 식품 중 중금속 최대기준 행정법규 개정 — 총 165개 기준 중 92개 신설·조정, 공포 후 약 6개월 유예
items.orig: Administrative Regulation No. 27/2026 Amendment to Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food"
items.products: Food
items.desc:
To further safeguard public health, enhance the efficiency of risk management, and promote harmonization between local regulations and international standards, the Macao Special Administrative Region Government has amended Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food". This amendment is based on the latest standards recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC), as well as those  established by major food-supplying countries and regions. This regulation has been scrutinized through risk assessment to ensure that it adequately protect public health in Macao, China.The revised regulation establishes a total of 165 maximum limits (MLs) for specified heavy metal contaminants in specific food items, of which 92 MLs represent optimizations or new additions. 
A reasonable transition period of approximately 6 months will be granted following the official promulgation of the regulation. This will provide sufficient time for the food industry to adapt its importation and safety control processes, and for local testing laboratories to establish and validate the necessary analytical capabilities in accordance with the new requirements.

items.ko: 땅콩 아플라톡신 의무기준 부합 인정 국제규격 목록 개정 — FSSC 22000 6.0 추가
items.orig: Notification of the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards Re: List of International Standards Complying with Mandatory Standards (No. 2)
items.products: Peanut (HS Code: 1202; ICS Code: 67.060)
items.desc:
Whereas it is deemed appropriate to amend the Notification of the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards Re: List of International Standards Complying with Mandatory Standards, dated 27 November B.E. 2568 (2025), due to the recognition of additional international standards aligned with the requirements of the Ministerial Regulation Establishing Agricultural Commodity Standard for Peanut Kernels: Maximum Level for Aflatoxin as Mandatory Standard B.E. 2558 (2015);The following provision shall be added as (e) under Clause 2 (1) of the Notification of the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards Re: List of International Standards Complying with Mandatory Standards, dated 27 November B.E. 2568 (2025):
"(e) Food Safety System Certification Scheme (Food Safety System Certification: FSSC 22000) Version 6.0 issued by The Foundation for Food Safety System Certification".Therefore, the international standards conforming to the Ministerial Regulation on the Establishment of Thai Agricultural Standard on Peanut Kernel: Maximum Level of Aflatoxin as mandatory standard B.E. 2558 (2015) are as follows:1. The system standards or production system standards, namely:(a) Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) complied with Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene or equivalent;(b) Hazards Analysis and Critical Control Point System (HACCP) complied with Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene or equivalent;(c) Food Safety Management System (FSMS) complied with ISO/IEC 22000;(d) Global standard for Food Safety Issue 9. British Retail Consortium;(e) Food Safety System Certification: FSSC 22000 version 6.0 issued by The Foundation for Food Safety System Certification.2. Aflatoxin analytical standards established by a national organization or international organizations such as Codex Alimentarius (Codex), International Organization for Standardization (ISO), AOAC International (AOAC) or analytical methods published in manual or international journals or analytical methods with the validation results obtained through the acknowledge procedures.This notification shall come into force on the date of its announcement (5 October 2026).

items.products: Milk and milk product (ICS code: 67.100)
items.note: 같은 개정안을 TBT로도 통보(G/TBT/N/THA/828)
items.desc: This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk" (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection
items.eif: The day following the date of its publication in the Government Gazette.

items.orig: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. …, issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: “Cow’s Milk” (No. 3)
items.products: Milk and milk product (ICS code: 67.100)
items.note: 같은 개정안을 TBT로도 통보(G/TBT/N/THA/829)
items.desc: This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk" (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.c. Amend the name designations of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk"  to align with the raw materials used.
items.eif: The day following the date of its publication in the Government Gazette.

items.orig: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives
items.products: Food additives
items.desc: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/SPS/N/TUR/126 on 20/06/2022. The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: 13 October 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonized with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.•    The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.•    E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.•    For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.•    E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.•     E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.•    The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabiliz
