items.orig: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation concerning the non-renewal of the approval of the active substance phenmedipham in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and amending Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 540/2011
items.products: Phenmedipham (pesticide active substance)
items.desc: This draft Commission Implementing Regulation provides that the approval of the active substance phenmedipham is not renewed in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. Member States shall withdraw authorisations for plant protection products containing phenmedipham as an active substance. The non-renewal of approval is based on the first evaluation of the substance for use as a pesticide active substance in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. The substance was formerly assessed and approved under Directive 91/414/ EEC.This decision only concerns the placing on the market of this substance and plant protection products containing it. Following non-approval and the expiry of all grace periods for stocks of products containing this substance, separate action will be taken on MRLs and a separate notification will be made in accordance with SPS procedures.
items.eif: 20 days following publication in the Official Journal of the EU

items.orig: Proposal P1067 – Health Star Rating System: 2nd Call for Submissions and Supporting Documents.
items.products: Imported and domestically produced packaged foods for retail sale in Australia and New Zealand that are required to bear a label, subject to certain exemptions and prohibitions.
items.desc: FSANZ has prepared a proposed draft amendment to the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (the Code) to mandate the display of a Health Star Rating (HSR) symbol on food for sale in Australia and New Zealand. The 2nd call for submissions provides FSANZ’s assessment and the proposed draft amendment, which would require the HSR to be calculated using a prescribed algorithm and the HSR symbol to be displayed on the front of most packaged foods for retail sale that are required to bear a nutrition information panel, subject to specified exemptions and prohibitions.  FSANZ seeks submissions on the proposed regulatory approach to inform its final assessment and a decision on whether to approve, amend or reject the proposed draft amendment.
items.adopt: Notification to Australian and New Zealand Government anticipated May 2027 with adoption (gazettal) to follow shortly after, pending Government consideration.
items.eif: A three-year transition period has been proposed beginning on the date of gazettal, with a further two-year stock-in-trade period.

items.desc: These declarations of special measures are necessary to prevent the incursion of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) to the United Kingdom. The measures prohibit the import of hay and straw and certain animal by-products from animals susceptible to foot-and-mouth disease from any countries, or zones within countries, that are not recognised by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) as free of foot-and-mouth disease – either with or without vaccination. Furthermore, it lays down phytosanitary requirements for import and internal movement of plants, plant products and other objects that may pose a phytosanitary risk to the European Union.This draft amendment of Implementing Regulation 2019/2072:Delists Aleurocanthus spiniferus, Raspberry leaf curl virus, and Strawberry leaf curl virus as quarantine pests and repeals measures associated with these pests.Lists the following species as quarantine pests and sets, where applicable, measures to avoid their entry and spread in the Union territory: Chloridea virescens, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4, Spodoptera ornithogalli, Spodoptera praefica, and Xanthomonas citri pv. viticolaPlease note that Chloridea virescens and Spodoptera ornithogalli were already listed in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1941 as species that are not to be introduced into, moved within, held, multiplied or released in the Union territory.Updates  requirements for import and internal movement, including addition/revision of the respective CN codes, for Agrilus planipennis, Hirschmanniella spp., Meloidogyne enterolobii, and Thaumatotibia leucotretaLists Toumeyella parvicornis as regulated non-quarantine pest and sets measure to avoid its spread in the Union.Introduces changes to the protected zones in relation to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus and Erwinia amylovora.Clarifies and corrects some inconsistencies (e.g. change of scientific names).

note.lead: 이번 주 식품 관련 통보 46건에서 눈여겨볼 흐름은 다섯 가지입니다.

themes.title: 우리나라가 건강기능식품 기준 개정안 등 4건을 통보했습니다
themes.text: 「건강기능식품의 기준 및 규격」 개정안 2건(체계 정비·영양성분 원료 확대, 기능성 원료 공통 제조기준 강화·녹차추출물 등 섭취 주의사항 개정)과 「식품등의 한시적 기준 및 규격 인정 기준」 개정안, GMO 안전성 심사 규정 개정안을 통보했습니다. 건강기능식품·한시적 기준 개정안의 의견 제출 기한은 2027년 1월 초입니다.

themes.title: 미국과 인도가 영유아식품 기준을 손봅니다
themes.text: 미국 FDA는 조제분유 필수 영양성분 4종의 최소·최대량을 조정하는 개정안을 냈고, 인도는 6개월 이하 영아용 식품의 당 함량 관련 규정 개정안을 통보했습니다. 인도는 차(茶) 중 아세타미프리드·이미다클로프리드 잔류허용기준 신설안도 함께 냈습니다.

themes.title: 캐나다가 식품첨가물·보충성분 목록 개정 5건을 통보했습니다
themes.text: 보충식품 허용 성분에 비타민 B6·셀레늄 관련 개정안을 냈고, 과일·채소 셀룰로스 분리물과 효소 2종을 허용하는 안, 분사제 2종을 첨가물 목록에서 삭제하는 안, 이산화규소 고결방지제 개정을 통보했습니다.

themes.title: 동아프리카 식품 표준 11종이 확정되고 6종이 새로 나왔습니다
themes.text: 동아프리카공동체가 2026년 6월 30일 육수·가금·콘비프·쇠고기 등급, 귀리·호밀·퀴노아·쌀가루 등 곡류 표준 11종을 채택했다고 알렸습니다. 땅콩기름·옥수수기름·마요네즈 등 표준안 6종도 새로 통보됐습니다.

themes.title: 앞서 통보된 규정이 확정·공포됐습니다
themes.text: 유럽연합은 4월에 통보한 식품접촉 재생 플라스틱 규정 개정을 규정 (EU) 2026/2376으로 채택했고, 튀르키예는 증류주 식품코덱스 고시를 공포했습니다. 인도네시아는 할랄제품 보증 정부령을 개정해 해외 할랄제품 적합성 보증 규정안을 폐지했습니다.

items.ko: 보충식품 허용 보충성분 목록 개정안(비타민 B6)
items.orig: Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients (vitamin B6)
items.products: Vitamin B6 as a supplemental ingredient
items.desc: Health Canada initiated an evaluation to determine whether revised conditions of use for vitamin B6 in supplemented foods should be proposed based on the publication of an updated scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level (UL) for vitamin B6 by the European Food Safety Authority Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (EFSA NDA Panel). Health Canada considered also considered control trials and case reports from the scientific literature, as well as information available in the Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database.The results of this evaluation support the revision of the conditions of use for vitamin B6 including the maximum permitted amounts in supplemented foods as well the threshold levels above which cautionary statements are required on the label.Therefore, Health Canada proposes modifying the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients, as described in the information document cited above.The purpose of this document is to publicly announce Health Canada’s intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit comments, inquiries or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.
items.adopt: The proposed modifications will be legally enabled once published in the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/food-nutrition/supplemented-foods/list-permitted-food-ingredients.html

Therefore, Health Canada proposes modifying the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients, as described in the information document.The purpose of this document is to publicly announce Health Canada's intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit comments, inquiries or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

items.desc: The proposed amendments seek to:A. Reorganization of the structural framework of the Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods (Draft Articles I.2, I.3, I.4, I.5, II.1, II.2, II.3, II.4, II.6, and [Annex 4])The provisions for "Collection and Handling of Test Samples" were separated from the general standards and specifications, and "Raw Materials" was relocated to the general manufacturing standards, alongside the removal of unnecessary details and clarification of provisions.B. items.orig: Proposal to modify the Table of Chemical, Physical and the Nutritional Characteristics of Food
items.products: Prepackaged food products (ICS: 67.230)
items.desc: Health Canada’s Food and Nutrition Directorate has launched a consultation regarding the notice of proposal to modify the Table of Chemical, Physical and Nutritional Characteristics of Food (Table).The Food and Drug Regulations (FDR) include requirements related to protein quality that apply to the conditions for making protein content statements and claims and to the composition of foods in certain categories. The Table sets out the values (for example, protein ratings) and corresponding method(s) of analysis for demonstrating compliance with the these requirements. The “Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score” (DIAAS) method is not currently permitted to demonstrate compliance with these protein quality requirements. The “Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score” (PDCAAS) method is permitted, however the prescribed methodology does not permit the use of protein digestibility values derived from in vitro assays (that is, non-human/animal). As described in the notice, Health Canada is proposing to authorize the use of the DIAAS method and two in vitro assays to determine protein digestibility values when using the PDCAAS method.The modifications to the Table would come into force the day they are published on Health Canada’s website and would include:the listing of the DIAAS method in the Table;the incorporation by reference into the FDR (through the Table) of the document Determination of the protein rating using the Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score (DIAAS); and the modifications to the incorporated by reference document Determination of the protein rating using the Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score (PDCAAS)
items.adopt: The proposed modifications will be legally enabled once published in Health Canada’s Table of Chemical, Physical and Nutritional Characteristics of Food, which is incorporated by reference into the Food and Drug Regulations: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/food-nutrition/legislation-guidelines/acts-regulations/incorporation-reference/table-chemical-physical-nutritional-characteristics-food.html

items.desc: Government Regulation No. 40 of 2026 amending Government Regulation No. 42 of 2024 on the Implementation of Halal Product Assurance revises Articles 160 and 161 concerning the phased implementation of mandatory halal certification.Article 160 extends the phase-in period for food, beverages, slaughter products and slaughtering services provided by micro and small enterprises until 17 October 2028. Mandatory halal certification for these products and services originating from abroad begins on 18 October 2028, taking into consideration the completion of mutual recognition arrangements for halal certificates. For medium and large enterprises, certification of related services, excluding slaughtering services, also begins on 18 October 2028. Paragraph (4) is deleted.Article 161 extends the phase-in period until 17 October 2028 for natural medicines, quasi-drugs, health supplements, cosmetics, chemical and genetically engineered products, specified consumer goods and Class A medical devices. The deadlines remain 17 October 2029 for over-the-counter and limited over-the-counter medicines and Class B medical devices, and 17 October 2034 for prescription medicines excluding psychotropics, and Class C medical devices. Related services follow the schedules of the respective products, and businesses may apply for certification before the applicable phase-in period ends.Pursuant to Article II, the provisions governing the assurance of conformity of foreign halal products entering the territory of Indonesia are repealed and declared no longer in force. Consequently, Regulation of the Halal Product Assurance Organizing Agency (BPJPH) No. 4 of 2026 on the Assurance of Conformity of Foreign Halal Products Entering the Territory of Indonesia, previously notified under G/TBT/N/IDN/190 and G/TBT/N/IDN/190/Add.1, is repealed and no longer in force.

items.orig: Resolución 00021295 del 28 de octubre de 2026, "Por medio de la cual se suspende temporalmente la emisión de documentos zoosanitarios de importación (DZI) para aves vivas, productos y subproductos de riesgo susceptibles de transmitir la enfermedad de Newcastle, procedentes del estado de Santa Catarina, Brasil y se dictan otras disposiciones" (Resolution No. 00021295 of 28 October 2026 temporarily suspending the issuance of animal health import documents (DZI) for live birds, products and by-products at risk of transmitting Newcastle disease, coming from the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil, and
items.products: Live birds, products and by-products posing a risk
items.desc: The notified Resolution temporarily suspends the issuance of animal health import documents (DZI) for live birds, products and by-products at risk of transmitting Newcastle disease, coming from the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil. If live birds or products and by-products of avian origin arrive in the country, the consignment shall be reshipped or destroyed, as appropriate. Entry into the country is also prohibited for such products when covered by animal health import documents (DZI) issued by the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) before the entry into force of the notified Resolution.
items.eif: 29 October 2026. The Resolution was published in Official Journal No. 53.673 of 29 October 2026 and entered into force the same day.

items.orig: Implementation Guide on the Updated Regulations on the Importation of Dogs and Cats into the Philippines
items.products: Live animals (excl. mammals, reptiles, birds, insects, fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic invertebrates and cultures of micro-organisms, etc.) (HS code(s): 010690)
items.note: 식품 관련성 낮음
items.desc: This Circular is hereby issued to provide the updated guidelines and implementation procedures for the importation of dogs and cats into the Philippines. It outlines the documentary and animal health requirements, including the approved Sanitary and Phytosanitary Import Clearance (SPSIC), rabies vaccination, parasite treatment, microchip identification, and among others. It must be noted that Philippines now requires Rabies Neutralizing Antibody Titer Test Result for each dog and cat entering the Philippines. Furthermore, Form 1 (Certificate of Animal Vaccination, Antibody Titer and Medication) is a mandatory document required during the application of SPSIC. This Circular also specifies the application process, required documents upon arrival, implementation schedule.

items.ko: 이집트산 생과 오렌지 수입 식물검역요건 결의안
items.orig: Establece requisitos fitosanitarios de importación para frutos frescos para consumo de naranja (citrus sinensis) procedentes de Egipto
items.products: Frutos frescos para consumo de naranja (citrus sinensis) Procedentes de Egipto
items.desc: El proyecto de resolución establece los requisitos fitosanitarios para la importación a Chile de frutos frescos para consumo de naranja ( Citrus sinensis ) de origen y procedencia Egipto. La medida establece que los envíos deberán estar amparados por un Certificado Fitosanitario Oficial emitido por la Organización Nacional de Protección Fitosanitaria de Egipto, incluyendo declaraciones adicionales para las plagas cuarentenarias asociadas a la vía. Para el manejo del riesgo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata se establece la aplicación de un tratamiento cuarentenario de frío T107-L, a una temperatura de 1,67 °C o inferior durante 18 días, el cual podrá realizarse en origen o en tránsito. Asimismo, se establecen medidas fitosanitarias específicas para Phytophthora palmivora y requisitos de inspección para las restantes plagascuarentenarias reguladas.Los envíos deberán proceder de lugares de producción y empacadoras registrados y autorizados por la autoridad fitosanitaria oficial de Egipto, identificados mediante códigos únicos, y deberán cumplir requisitos de trazabilidad que permitan relacionar cada lote con su lugar de producción, empacadora, Certificado Fitosanitario, contenedor y sello o precinto, según corresponda. La propuesta contempla además requisitos de muestreo e inspección fitosanitaria, limpieza, lavado y cepillado de los frutos, ausencia de flores, hojas, restos vegetales y suelo, condiciones de embalaje, rotulación, resguardo y transporte, así como inspección fitosanitaria por el Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero al ingreso a Chile. Previo al inicio de la primera temporada de exportación, el SAG realizará una verificación técnica en origen destinada a evaluar el cumplimiento de los requisitos establecidos, las condiciones de los lugares de producción y empacadoras, los procedimientos oficiales de certificación fitosanitaria y el programa de vigilancia y monitoreo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata.Para mayor detalle, revisar el documento adjunto a esta notificación.
items.eif: Por definir.
